**DONGRYEOLLEE1** (2026-08-28T04:40:51Z):

**2× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) data point: NVFP4 with the FP8 PLE table kept on GPU (no CPU offload), a second engine co-hosted on the same two cards, and confirmation that the prefix-caching `align` promotion fires on the NVIDIA image.**

Setup: 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (96 GB, SM120), driver 580.173 / CUDA 13.0, RunPod secure-cloud pod (container without `--privileged`, see [my comment on #53899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53899#issuecomment-5448518741) for why the offload cannot be used there), image `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` (`0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198`), `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, `--quantization modelopt --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --disable-custom-all-reduce --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' --compilation-config '{"mode":"NONE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4,8,12,16]}'`, env `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, BF16 KV. Thanks to net-snix, SirTificate and OsakaTX: the custom-allreduce and BF16-KV findings and the `_get_ple_embedding_quant_method` escape hatch (`VLLM_PLE_FORCE_FP8=1`) are theirs; without the latter the ModelOpt config never reaches the FP8 PLE path and loading stops at `ngram_embedding.weight_scale`.

## 1. NVFP4 + FP8 PLE table resident on GPU

The thread has NVFP4 with offload (SirTificate) and FP8 with the table on GPU (net-snix); this is the remaining combination. Per rank:

|                                                                   | measured                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| resident weights: NVFP4 experts + BF16 dense + FP8 PLE shard      | 66.1 GiB (40.5 + 25.6)                                              |
| `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.76` → KV pool                         | 239,238 tokens, 1.83× concurrency at 131,072                        |
| weight load / CUDA-graph capture (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, sizes 4-16) | 285 s / 7 s, 0.31 GiB                                               |
| single stream, 512-token completions, through the HTTPS proxy     | 122-126 tok/s                                                       |
| MTP k=3 acceptance over ~2.5k drafts (mixed chat + code)          | 51.0 % (per position 69 / 48 / 36 %), 2.53 accepted tokens per step |

Outputs were checked for content (Korean QA with reasoning split by `qwen3`, code generation, a `qwen3_xml` tool call returning `get_weather({"city": "서울"})`), not only for the absence of errors.

## 2. Two engines on the same two cards

The remaining budget runs a second vLLM engine, `Qwen3.8-27B` NVFP4 (compressed-tensors) TP=2 with its own MTP k=3, at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.19`: 143,945 KV tokens at 65,536, 85-86 tok/s single stream, 54.6 % MTP acceptance. Total 0.95 utilization, 91.1 GB used per card. One thing that cost us a restart: at 0.15 the 27B engine loaded weights and profiled activations to 14.15 GiB and ended with 0.15 GiB for KV, which fails the "at least one max-length request" check (1.15 GiB needed at 65,536); 0.18-0.19 with `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` is the floor on this card for that pairing.

## 3. Prefix caching: the `align` promotion does fire on this image

Re the dolf3131 (GB10, arm64 image) / zzw09773 (ROCm) disagreement: on `8e685d198` x86_64 with only `--enable-prefix-caching` passed, startup logs

```
Mamba cache mode is set to 'align' for Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration by default when prefix caching is enabled
```

so the hybrid-model hook in `model_executor/models/config.py` runs here, and a 1,600-token attention block is what you get. The "inert without `--mamba-cache-mode align`" observation therefore looks specific to the arm64/GB10 image rather than to the branch.

Not verified: the per-token cost of keeping the table on GPU versus offloading it; our tok/s include proxy round-trip and prefill and are not directly comparable to the local 149-161 tok/s numbers above.

**jschmied** (2026-08-28T09:37:51Z):

**`lm_head` cannot be quantized on this model, and one of the three reasons is in this PR's own
model file — worth a one-line change before merge.**

`lm_head` is BF16 `[248320, 2560]` in every published GPU checkpoint of Flash-Next (verified across
ten). That is not a checkpoint choice. Three independent things block it, and any one alone is
sufficient:

**1. This PR's model file never passes `quant_config` to `ParallelLMHead`.**

`vllm/models/qwen3_8_flash_next/nvidia/model.py`:

```python
self.lm_head = ParallelLMHead(
  config.vocab_size,
  config.hidden_size,
  prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, 'lm_head'),  # <- no quant_config
)
```

`VocabParallelEmbedding.__init__` then sees `quant_config is None` and installs
`UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` unconditionally — `get_quant_method` is never called, so a checkpoint
declaring `lm_head` in `quantized_layers` is silently ignored. `self.quant_config` is already in
scope two lines up, and `ParallelLMHead` already accepts the kwarg:

```python
quant_config = (self.quant_config,)
```

Same in `mtp.py`, which constructs its own `ParallelLMHead` the same way.

**2 and 3 are not this PR's** — recording them so the picture is complete. `config.json`'s
`quantization_config.ignore` contains `lm_head` in the checkpoints we tested (so `is_layer_excluded`
returns early), and `VocabParallelEmbedding`'s vocab-aware loader asserts
`loaded_weight.shape[output_dim] == self.org_vocab_size`, which is true of `weight` and false of a
block-scale companion shaped `[1940, 20]` — the embedding loader has no notion of a scale tensor.
We worked around the third locally by attaching a plain copy loader to the scale parameters, with
an explicit `NotImplementedError` for TP>1 since the scale would need sharding in _block_ space.

**Why it is worth supporting: measured on one GB10, TP=1.**

|           | `lm_head` BF16 | `lm_head` FP8 blockwise |
| --------- | -------------: | ----------------------: |
| code      |     23.2 tok/s |                **26.1** |
| factual   |     23.7 tok/s |                **26.2** |
| NLL/token |         0.9687 |              **0.9628** |
| tasks     |          10/10 |                   10/10 |

Paired NLL over 14 chunks / 646 tokens of held-out prose, code, German, French and technical text;
9 chunks better and 5 worse, so we read the −0.6% as noise and report it as **no measurable
quality cost**, not as an improvement. **+11% decode** matches a bandwidth model: at `[248320,
2560]` the head is 1.27 GB read on every token, of a ~7.25 GB per-token budget.

Format matters more than the layer: on the sibling Qwen3.8-27B we previously measured an **NVFP4**
head at 2.4% worse NLL and declined it, while an **FP8** head is loss-neutral.

One prefix note for anyone implementing: vLLM asks about **`language_model.lm_head`**, not
`lm_head`, so a config keyed on the bare name still resolves (the candidate list handles it) but is
worth testing explicitly:

```python
c = ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.from_config(
  json.load(open('config.json'))['quantization_config']
)
c.is_layer_excluded('language_model.lm_head')  # must be False
c._resolve_quant_algo('language_model.lm_head')  # must be the algo you wrote
```

That ten-second offline check would have saved us three ten-minute boot cycles.

Happy to send the one-line `quant_config` change as a PR against this branch if useful — the other
two are separate and belong upstream of the model.

**abtraore** (2026-08-28T21:51:34Z):

We implemented the FP8 main-KV path this PR leaves gated (`kv_quant_mode` is plumbed but every gate raises "Qwen4Exp QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache") and validated it on consumer Blackwell. Patch against this PR's lineage (the `qwen38-flash-next` nightly): https://gist.github.com/abtraore/329547468a6eb04ecedac38250148093 — happy to turn it into a PR against this branch, or as a follow-up once this merges.

**Design** (mirrors the shipped DeepSeek-V4 `fp8_ds_mla` split of quantized attended-values / dequant-on-read):

- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` accepted through the five config gates; the parent `FlashAttentionImpl` FA capability probe is bypassed by handing it `"auto"` and restoring the dtype after `super().__init__()` — QSA never runs flash-attn over the cache, so the probe does not apply.
- Write path is unchanged upstream code: the inherited `reshape_and_cache_flash` already quantizes given the dtype string and the layer's registered scales.
- Read path: the uint8 pages are viewed as `float8_e4m3fn` after the K/V split, and the splitk Triton kernel gains an `IS_FP8: tl.constexpr` — e4m3→bf16 upcast before each `tl.dot` (sm12x cannot dot fp8 operands), K-scale folded into the existing logit scaling, V-scale into the final normalize. Scales are read from the on-device `layer._k_scale/_v_scale` buffers, so CUDA-graph replay stays valid.
- The indexer side-cache stays bf16 (it already ignores `cache_dtype_str`), so block selection precision is untouched — strictly more conservative than DeepSeek's shipped fp4 indexer cache.

**Validation** (4× RTX 5090 32 GB, sm120, TP=4 + EP, RadixArk NVFP4 checkpoint, MTP n=3; experiment → result):

1. Boot, bf16 baseline → KV pool 389,084 tokens (1.48× at 262,144).
2. Same boot with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` → pool **692,910 tokens (+78%)**; attention block re-equalizes 800→1600 against the mamba page as expected.
3. Greedy A/B, four prompts, bf16 vs fp8 → final content **md5-identical** on every prompt.
4. Decode: 170 tok/s shallow / 211 on code (≥ bf16's 169/203); 186–207 tok/s at 115K–224K context. MTP acceptance unchanged (0.68–0.93 across workloads).
5. Prefill at 115–186K: 2,350–2,490 tok/s vs 2,551–2,690 bf16 (−8%, quantize-on-write).
6. Needle retrieval through fp8-scored QSA selection: 3/3 at ~140K (depths 10/50/95%).
7. The larger pool enables what bf16 cannot boot: `--max-model-len 393216` with YaRN 1.5 (bf16 pool 389,084 < 393,216 refuses) → pool 720,159, needle 3/3 at 336K, drafter acceptance 0.74–0.90 past native with `max_model_len` pinned inside `--speculative-config`.

One note for the eventual first-party version: with CPU offload enabled, the PLE offload worker's CUDA context also breaks the `--kv-cache-memory` boot advisory — filed separately with a fix in #54275.

**AI assistance disclosure** (per the contributing policy): developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5 via Claude Code). Procedure: kernel-path recon of this PR's `qsa.py`/`ops/qsa.py`, study of the in-tree DSV4 `fp8_ds_mla` precedent, patch, then the gated validation above on live hardware. The human submitter reviewed the patch and owns the results.

**jschmied** (2026-08-29T17:56:37Z):

**A second `quant_config` hole, and a branch with both fixes applied to this PR's head.**

`nvidia/hyperconnection.py` hardcodes `quant_config=None` on all three `GatedResidual`
projections (lines 102, 113, 122 at `91a6b555`), so the hyper-connection linears are always
unquantized regardless of what the checkpoint declares. The class docstring twelve lines above
states the opposite:

> ...are vLLM Linear modules (merged replicated linear for down+inject), so GEMM dispatch
> (e.g. the low-latency skinny GEMM) applies through the standard `quant_method` mechanism.

It cannot, because `quant_method` is only ever `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for these layers. The
three call sites in `model.py` already have a `quant_config` in scope (the mixer site needs
`vllm_config.quant_config`).

Branch against this PR's head, rebased onto `91a6b555`, three commits, 12 insertions:
https://github.com/jschmied/vllm/tree/gb10-sm121-fixes

1. `GatedResidual` takes and forwards `quant_config`
2. `quant_config` on both `ParallelLMHead` sites — the `lm_head` case from my earlier comment
   (`mtp.py` uses `self.quant_config`, since the drafter resolves its own via
   `get_draft_quant_config()` and the two differ whenever `ignore` carries `mtp.*`)
3. The `MIXED_PRECISION` dispatch gap for `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` — that one also affects
   `main`, so it is filed separately as #54367 rather than carried here

**One honest caveat on (1).** We converted 96 hyper-connection `_up` projections to per-channel
FP8 on a GB10 and it was **performance-neutral**: 36.05 vs 36.45 tok/s, n=6 per arm from empty
compile caches, against a measured 6.9% noise floor. A per-shape microbenchmark explains why —
`(10240, 320)` at M≤8 runs 30.8 us against a 24.0 us roofline, i.e. already ~78% of peak, so it
is latency-bound and halving the bytes buys 1.18x; `(336, 10240)` is _slower_ in FP8 (0.89x). By
contrast `(10240, 2560)` gives 2.42x, which is why FP8 pays on the dense projections and not
here.

So (1) is a correctness/reachability fix, not a speed one: today a checkpoint that declares these
layers quantized is silently ignored. I would not want it merged on a performance argument I
cannot support.

**tsw2k** (2026-08-31T10:56:14Z):

Running this stack in a configuration you may not have tried: TP4 across four DGX Sparks (GB10, sm121), on the day-0 image. Repo with the launcher, patches and measurements: https://github.com/tsw2k/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quad-DGX-Sparks

The good news first: multi-node works. `--nnodes 4` with the mp backend rendezvouses fine, and at native 262k the fleet passes a full gate suite (concurrent ~30k prefills, byte-identical greedy decode, NIAH to 128k, vision, tool calls). 4.7M-token KV pool, 31 tok/s single stream, 157 tok/s aggregate at 16 streams.

Four findings that may be useful for this PR:

1. Plain TP4 cannot load the NVFP4 checkpoint. TP sharding cuts the MoE intermediate 640 to 160 per rank and FLASHINFER_CUTLASS raises `NotImplementedError: Intermediate size padding for w1 and w3`. `--enable-expert-parallel` avoids it. A clearer error message, or implying EP for this case, would save people a boot.

2. `_get_ple_embedding_quant_method` only accepts `Fp8Config`, so `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1` with the ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint dies loading `ngram_embedding.weight_scale`. The PLE shards are fp8 plus weight_scale either way; accepting `ModelOptNvFp4Config` there fixes it.

3. The PLE offload worker loads the whole table in one process. On a 128 GB GB10 node its load peak reached ~85 GB anon RSS (the fp8 table plus a temporary copy) and drew a global OOM kill at any gpu_memory_utilization we tried. The `nnodes != 1` check in `_validate_ple_offload_config` looks stricter than the architecture requires, since the worker is spawned per WorkerProc and its pidfd handover is node-local, but memory rather than topology is what stops it on this hardware.

4. The open bug: on the 1M YaRN lane, roughly the third request with a prompt over ~100k tokens hangs a worker's GPU stream. The `sample_tokens` RPC times out and the engine dies. `/health` is 200 until then, and short requests never trigger it. We eliminated, one variable per boot on a rebooted fleet: prefix caching, MTP, expandable_segments, page cache (an unconditional flusher through serving), chunk size 8192 down to 1024, CUDA graphs (`--enforce-eager` dies identically), and three different PLE paths (the blazux mmap patch, the resident vocab-sharded table, and CPU offload as far as it would go). py-spy shows every surviving rank parked at the first stream-sync point after the wedge, so the hang is in a kernel enqueued earlier in the forward: GDN, QSA or the EP all-to-all. Full isolation matrix and stack: https://github.com/tsw2k/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quad-DGX-Sparks/blob/main/docs/OPEN-PROBLEMS.md

Happy to run instrumented boots or share full logs if that helps.

**tsw2k** (2026-08-31T20:02:25Z):

One more data point for finding 4: the same failure shape has now been reported on a different engine. A withdrawn 2x GB10 SGLang profile for this checkpoint hit invalid sampling probabilities with CUDA asserts and Xid 43 under multi-turn agentic traffic, with the same trigger sequence of long prefill, decode, tool turn, longer prefill: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/381836

Two engines, one hardware platform, one traffic shape. Our runs add that the hang survives MTP=0, so speculative decoding is not required to trigger it. Together this points below the engine layer, toward shared kernels or numerics on sm121.
